steps.body: Two shapes are **congruent** when one can be moved onto the other using only rigid motions — translations, reflections, and rotations. Since those never change size or shape, congruent shapes are identical: same side lengths, same angles.
Flip and slide a triangle onto its target while comparing the original and image side lengths.

widget.prompt: Reflect the triangle, then slide it 5 units right until it matches the target image.
widget.successFeedback: The reflected and translated triangle matches the target exactly. Its position and orientation changed, but every side length and angle stayed the same.
widget.offsetFeedback: The orientation may be right, but the vertices are not on the target yet. Move every vertex by the same offset.
widget.reflectFeedback: The target reverses the triangle's left-right orientation. Turn on the reflection before adjusting the slide.

predict.prompt: What happens to a shape's side lengths when it is reflected?

options.label: They change because the shape is reversed

predict.reveal: Reflections, translations, and rotations are rigid motions. They can change position or orientation, but they preserve every length and angle.

steps.body: To show two shapes are congruent, describe a SEQUENCE of rigid motions that maps one exactly onto the other — for example, 'translate, then rotate.' If such a sequence exists, they're congruent.

explanationVariants: Congruent shapes have equal corresponding side lengths and equal corresponding angles.
Rigid motions preserve both lengths and angles, so congruent shapes match in both.

widget.prompt: If two triangles are congruent, what must be true?

options.label: Their side lengths and angles are all equal
options.feedback: Right — rigid motions preserve every length and angle.

options.label: Only their angles are equal
options.feedback: Congruence preserves SIDE LENGTHS too, not just angles.

options.label: Only their areas are equal
options.feedback: Congruent shapes match in every measurement — sides, angles, AND area.

options.label: They must be the same color
options.feedback: Color isn't a geometric property — congruence is about equal sides and angles.

widget.prompt: Triangle A is at the top-left; congruent triangle B is at the bottom-right, turned. How do you map A to B?

panels.title: First
panels.body: Translate A across to B's position — a slide handles the location.

panels.title: Then
panels.body: Rotate to match B's turned orientation — a turn handles the facing.

panels.title: Result
panels.body: Translate, then rotate — a sequence of rigid motions maps A exactly onto B, proving congruence.

widget.successFeedback: Exactly — a sequence of rigid motions is how you demonstrate congruence.

explanationVariants: A shape and its enlargement are NOT congruent — enlarging changes the size, which rigid motions never do.
Resizing breaks congruence; only same-size shapes can be congruent.

widget.prompt: Shape B is shape A enlarged to twice the size. Are A and B congruent?

options.label: No — enlarging changes the size
options.feedback: Right — congruence requires the same size, and enlarging breaks that.

options.label: Yes — they're the same shape
options.feedback: Same shape isn't enough — congruence needs the same SIZE too, and B is bigger.

options.label: Yes — enlarging is a rigid motion
options.feedback: Enlarging is NOT rigid — it changes size, so the shapes aren't congruent.

options.label: Only if A is also flipped
options.feedback: Flipping wouldn't fix the size difference — B is twice as big, so they're not congruent.

explanationVariants: Two triangles with identical side lengths (3, 4, 5 each) are congruent — one maps onto the other by rigid motions.
Matching all side lengths means the shapes are congruent.

widget.prompt: Which pair of triangles must be congruent?

options.label: Both have sides 3, 4, 5
options.feedback: Right — identical side lengths mean one can be mapped onto the other by rigid motions.

options.label: One has sides 3,4,5; the other 6,8,10
options.feedback: Those are proportional (twice as big) — SIMILAR, but not congruent (different sizes).

options.label: Both are 'triangles'
options.feedback: Just being triangles isn't enough — congruence needs matching side lengths and angles.

options.label: Both are red
options.feedback: Color isn't geometric — congruence depends on equal sides and angles.

steps.body: Sort transformations by whether they keep congruence.
explanationVariants: Translations, reflections, rotations keep congruence (rigid). Enlarging/shrinking breaks it (changes size).
Rigid motions preserve congruence; resizing does not.

widget.prompt: Sort each transformation: does it keep the shape congruent?

items.label: slide 4 units up
items.feedback: A translation keeps size and shape — congruent.

items.label: reflect across a line
items.feedback: A reflection keeps size and shape — congruent.

items.label: rotate 90°
items.feedback: A rotation keeps size and shape — congruent.

items.label: enlarge to 3× the size
items.feedback: Enlarging changes the size — not congruent.

items.label: shrink to half the size
items.feedback: Shrinking changes the size — not congruent.

widget.missFeedback: Not quite — rigid motions (slide, flip, turn) keep congruence; resizing breaks it.
widget.successFeedback: All sorted — only size-changing transformations break congruence.

hints: Congruence needs the size AND shape to stay identical.
Slides, flips, and turns never change size — they keep congruence.
Enlarging or shrinking changes the size, so those break congruence.

steps.body: Congruent shapes are linked by a sequence of rigid motions — same size, same shape.
takeaways: Congruent = mappable by translations, reflections, rotations.
Congruent shapes have equal corresponding sides and angles.
Resizing breaks congruence; rigid motions preserve it.
steps.teaser: Next: dilations, which resize shapes on purpose.

concept.body: Two shapes are congruent when a sequence of rigid motions (translations, reflections, rotations) maps one onto the other. Congruent shapes have equal corresponding sides and angles.

explanationVariants: A shape slid and rotated is congruent to the original — rigid motions keep size and shape.
Sliding and turning are rigid, so the shapes stay congruent.

widget.prompt: Shape B is shape A slid 3 right and rotated 90°. Are they congruent?

options.label: Yes — only rigid motions were used
options.feedback: Right — sliding and turning keep size and shape.

options.label: No — rotating changes the shape
options.feedback: Rotation is rigid — it keeps size and shape, so they're congruent.

options.label: No — they're in different spots
options.feedback: Position doesn't affect congruence — rigid motions were used, so congruent.

options.label: Only if B is resized
options.feedback: Resizing would break congruence — since only rigid motions were used, they're congruent.
